topics.topic: Assignment of global store positions within transactions and on updates
questions: What exactly is the single store position, and what order is assigned to multiple records created in one transaction?
How are multiple new records written by the same store call ordered, and do updates to existing records receive a new position?
How is the position assigned when one transaction creates several records, and does updating an entity's status change its position?

quotes:
Activation M09 and FlowActivation M18 records are identified by their position
in the store's one order of records (K-17); a later activation of the same
implementation or flow version, after another was active, is a new record,
never the old one again; asking for the one already active records nothing
(A04 rules 4 and 5, A06 rule 4).

Only the store module opens the database. Every change is one call to the
store module and one transaction inside it; callers never open, name or pass a
transaction (K-17).

record_change: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Every record written gets one store position from a single strictly increasing counter shared by all record types, assigned inside the transaction that writes it; store order is the order of these positions, every collection the module returns is in store order unless the function says otherwise, and Activation and FlowActivation records are identified by their store_position.

record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.
judgement.divergence: One implementation assigns positions to newly created records in each change's payload/listing order; another assigns them by record type or database insertion order. Owners and agents notice different list and paging order, corpus order, and activation identities; later text does answer that updates retain the creation position.
judgement.why: The texts define one global counter and preserve positions on updates, but do not give a total position-assignment order for every combination of records newly created in one transaction.

topics.topic: Exact credential-file newline removal and forbidden control characters
questions: Exactly which trailing byte sequence is removed, how many occurrences are removed, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
What exactly counts as the one trailing newline, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
What exactly counts as the removable trailing newline and as a forbidden control character?

judgement.why: This is the same credential-newline and control-character question previously assigned to State 6, and its deciding passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Credential-file newline normalization and control-character validation
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Exact ownership and permission requirements for data-directory privacy
questions: What exact ownership and permission conditions define "private" for the data directory, its subdirectories and its files, and are ACLs or other users' execute permissions included?
What exact filesystem facts make the data directory and its contents private enough to start?
Which ownership and permission bits constitute “private,” and must the rule be checked recursively for directories as well as regular files?

quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
judgement.why: The later store contract requires the data directory and everything inside it to be owned by the effective user, grant no permission to group or others, and contain no followed or discovered symbolic link.

topics.topic: Finality, retry eligibility, and retry transitions for waiting mapped elements
questions: Which NodeExecution statuses make an element permanently concluded, and which leave it retryable despite its concluded attempt record?
Does a prior waiting-status NodeExecution prevent another attempt, or does "concluded" here mean only a terminal element conclusion rather than any concluded attempt record?
Does “concluded record” mean any NodeExecution, or only a record whose derived element conclusion is final, and how is a waiting element selected for its next attempt?
What are the complete transitions from each waiting status to retry, continued waiting, success or failure?

judgement.why: This is the same question about terminal conclusions, waiting elements, and retry eligibility already decided by the later run contracts.

precedent.topic: Which mapped-element execution outcomes are terminal conclusions versus retryable attempts
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity, its pinned graph with read_flow_version, and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, and derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status, an operation element from operation_element_conclusion. If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused. Otherwise it executes one node at a time until no node can execute, then writes the rest or end state in one RecordRunProgressChange.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract derives semantic conclusions from the trace, excludes waiting operation elements from ordinary advancement, forbids re-executing concluded elements, and classifies resolved `not_applied` as waiting for approval.

topics.topic: Security checks and failure handling for per-request configuration re-reads
questions: On a per-request token-list re-read, must the configuration file still pass A17's no-symlink, regular-file, ownership and permission checks, or only A16's four checks?
When the configuration is re-read before a request, must A17's file and path security checks run again, and what happens if they fail?
After startup, must every token-list re-read repeat A17's secure-open, ownership, type and permission checks, or may it accept tokens from a file that would fail A17 at startup?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which security checks are repeated during a live token-list reread.

precedent.topic: Repeating security checks when rereading the token-list configuration
quotes:
Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ,
   or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it (K-15) and takes from it only the
   token list.

Exactly four checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal; no two agent tokens share a name (M28).

Every other field of the configuration, and every other start check, applies
   only at a restart.
precedent.why: The live re-read applies exactly the four listed token checks, while the file-protection start checks apply only at restart.

topics.topic: Startup handling and creation of a missing data directory and required store objects
questions: May the data-directory path itself be a symbolic link, may the kernel create a missing directory, and which privacy checks occur before creating the lock or other files?
What does startup do for a new installation whose data directory or expected store objects do not yet exist?
If the configured data directory or its required subdirectories/database do not exist, does the kernel create them or refuse to start?

quotes: open_store: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError whose reason names the failed check: data_directory does not exist (it is never created here), lock held by another process, directory not private (naming the first offending path), or symbolic link found (naming its path); it removes and creates nothing when a check fails.

The kernel never
creates the data directory itself: the owner creates it, private to the
kernel's user; inside it `open_store` creates the database schema, the
content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
judgement.why: The later store API refuses a missing data directory but creates the database schema, content-addressed area, and spool area inside an existing valid directory.

topics.topic: Startup handling of invalid, repeated, unknown, or unreadable service-instance selections
questions: What happens at startup when the configuration repeats a service selection, selects an unknown service or instance, or the selected instance cannot be read from the configured manifest revision?
Does an unknown configured instance name stop kernel startup, count as no selected instance, or count as a selected instance whose address is missing?
What happens when configuration names an instance that does not exist in the configured manifest revision?

quotes:
Checks in this order, the first failing one named: a regular private file of
the kernel's user, not a link; one JSON object with exactly the installation's
fields; no service twice among the selected instances or among the credentials;
every credential header name an HTTP field-name token; every secret file
reference an absolute path; tokens of at least 43
characters; tokens pairwise distinct; agent names pairwise distinct (A16 rule 1,
A17 rule 1, M28).

The services checked are those the installation holds a credential for, in
   `service_id` order; for one it also selects an instance for, a manifest
   record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule
   5) stops the start naming it; a selected instance
   the record does not list fails nothing here
   (it is not invocable at send, A09 rule 6).
judgement.why: The later startup texts refuse repeated service selections, define when unreadable manifest records stop startup, and state that a selected instance absent from its record does not stop startup but is uninvocable at send.

topics.topic: Definition of total arrival order for concurrent surface requests
questions: What defines arrival order when multiple MCP requests are received concurrently or in the same transport event?
What event establishes the total order between requests received concurrently or through different connections?

quotes: serve_kernel: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Requests are handled strictly one at a time, each to its end, run advancement included, before the next one is read (A18 rule 3).
judgement.why: The later surface contract establishes the total order by reading no next request until the current request has completed.

topics.topic: Legality and wire encoding of non-ASCII credential HTTP header values
questions: How is a non-ASCII UTF-8 credential value represented on the HTTP wire, or must such a value be refused before sending?
Which decoded credential values are legal HTTP header values, and how are non-ASCII characters encoded on the wire?

judgement.why: This is the same question about legal credential header values and non-ASCII wire serialization already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Valid credential HTTP-header values and non-ASCII wire serialization
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Ordering of newly non-executable conclusions relative to ready-node execution
questions: After an execution changes reachability, must all newly skipped or upstream-failed nodes be recorded before another ready node executes, after ready execution is exhausted, or interleaved by one common node order?

When propagation makes some nodes skipped or upstream_failed while other nodes are ready, are all non-executable conclusions recorded first, are ready nodes executed first, or are both kinds processed in one node_id order; and what exactly makes conclusions occur “together”?

judgement.why: This is the same question about propagation of newly non-executable records before selection of another executable node.

precedent.topic: Ordering of non-executable-node propagation versus ready-node execution
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Rollback of files published before a later symbolic-link failure
questions: If a store call publishes a file and subsequently encounters a symbolic link, must the published file be removed, or is the orphan-file exception allowed?
May a store call that later encounters a symbolic link leave files it published earlier in that call, or must it roll them back so literally nothing was written?

quotes:
Every
file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at
start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call
fail with nothing written.
judgement.why: The specific symbolic-link rule requires that call to fail with nothing written, so its earlier publications may not remain.

topics.topic: Atomic validation and commitment of multi-output node results
questions: For an ordinary node with several outputs, must all outputs pass schema and size checks before any output is stored or delivered, or may earlier outputs remain when a later output fails?

topics.topic: Crash-consistent ordering between content-file publication and record commit
questions: What ordering and recovery rule guarantees that a committed record can never name a file that was not durably published when a crash occurs between file publication and the SQLite commit?

topics.topic: Equality semantics used for guard values
questions: What equality relation is used for guard values, especially for JSON numbers such as `1` and `1.0`, objects with different member order, and strings with canonically equivalent Unicode?

topics.topic: Handling duplicate credential entries for the same service
questions: How is a configuration containing two credential entries for the same service handled, and does equality of their contents change the result?

topics.topic: Handling mismatched content at an existing digest-derived file path
questions: What happens when a file already exists at a digest-derived location but its bytes or size differ from the bytes now being published under that digest?

topics.topic: Mapped-node scan behavior when resuming after a wait
questions: On a later request, does the mapped node scan all elements again in list order, operate only on the specifically unblocked element, or resume from the position where the earlier pass ended?

topics.topic: Precedence among multiple startup validation failures
questions: Which startup failure is reported first when, for example, the configuration permissions, token list, credential header, data directory and sandbox probe are all invalid?

topics.topic: Release version whose size limit governs existing mapped-list conclusions
questions: Which release's stored_value_bytes_max is used to derive an existing run's mapped-list conclusion after an upgrade?

topics.topic: Representation of unproduced flow outputs while a run is resting
questions: While a run is resting, are unproduced flow-output ports omitted, included with a nonfinal reason, or included with another placeholder?

topics.topic: Scope of symbolic-link prohibitions throughout the data-directory tree
questions: Does the prohibition include symbolic links used as directories, the data-directory path itself, SQLite sidecar files and every recursively nested entry?

topics.topic: Startup behavior when cleanup of temporary or unreferenced files fails
questions: What happens if startup cannot remove a temporary file or an unreferenced value byte?

topics.topic: Storage, tracing, failure-detail, and logging rules for request tokens
questions: What exact storage, tracing, failure-detail and logging prohibitions apply to the owner and agent tokens received with requests?

topics.topic: Treatment of orphan spool files belonging to unfinished runs
questions: After restart, do unnamed files in an unfinished run's spool count toward `spool_run_bytes_max`, get removed, or remain ignored until their exact position is reused?

topics.topic: Whether startup recovery may advance execution or send messages
questions: Is startup recovery an accepted exception to the earlier invariant, or must it only reconstruct state and wait for a later request before executing or sending anything?

topics.topic: Which related store mutations must be committed atomically
questions: Which related mutations constitute one indivisible change—for example a function conclusion, its values and NodeExecution, approval creation plus waiting state, and run status or waiting-point updates?
